newsitem.title: USA: Florida city calm after more race riots.
newsitem.headline: Florida city calm after more race riots.

text.p: Calm returned to a poor black neighbourhood on Thursday morning after a night of shooting and arson triggered by a grand jury's decision to clear a white police officer of killing a black youth.

Police in riot gear used tear gas overnight to disperse small groups of angry youths who opened fire, threw rocks and torched buildings. At least five people were hurt in the second bout of racial violence in the Florida city in a month.
One police officer was shot in the leg and another in a helicopter was grazed by a bullet. Three civilians were also injured, according to local television reports.

"Everything's calm right now," an officer at police headquarters said on Thursday morning. She was unable to give The unrest followed a decision by a grand jury that police officer James Knight was justified in shooting Tyron Lewis, 18, after he pulled Lewis' car over for speeding on Oct. 24. That shooting sparked a night of rioting in which 11 people were hurt and about 30 shops, businesses or homes set ablaze.

Much of Wednesday's violence broke out near headquarters of a black activist group, the National People's Democratic Uhuru Movement. The group, already under investigation by federal prosecutors for its role in last month's riot, advocates using violence to create a separate black society.
The Uhuru group, named after a Swahili word for "freedom," recently called for the execution of St. Petersburg's police chief and mayor after conducting its own trial.

"We've had threats, constant threats for the past two weeks, saying that if the report from the grand jury didn't meet with their satisfaction that the town was going to burn," Police Chief Darrel Stephens told reporters.

City officials said the group showed little signs of willingness to help negotiate a solution to the complaints of many black citizens, who claim they have been victimised by police, a lack of jobs and bleak prospects for years.

Prosecutors said the 16 grand jurors, only one of whom was black, had determined Lewis' death "was the result of a justifiable homicide." The jury said Knight was in danger of being run over by the car Lewis was driving after he and his partner, Sandra Minor, pulled Lewis over for speeding.
